quizzes.title: NEET-UG 2026 cancellation: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: NEET 2026 was declared compromised amid allegations of a paper leak. Authorities initiated an investigation after reports surfaced about illicit paper leaks and the circulation of unauthorised exam material. Evidence uncovered by law enforcement formed part of the investigation, and the decision reflects a commitment to fairness in high-stakes academic evaluations across the country. NEET is the national entrance examination for admission into medical colleges across India. Exam cancellations delay admissions and disrupt the academic calendar for millions of students. Re-conducting compromised examinations imposes a heavy financial burden on government institutions. The Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act 2024 was introduced to curb paper leaks, organised cheating and manipulation in recruitment and entrance examinations. Investigations under the Act are conducted by officers not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police or Assistant Commissioner of Police. Offences under the Act are cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable. The scope of unfair means includes leakage of question papers or answer keys, candidate impersonation, unauthorised assistance during examinations, and tampering with computer systems or networks. The Central Government may transfer investigations to a Central Investigating Agency when required. Unfair practices cause significant stress, frustration and demotivation for ethical students. Large-scale cheating causes parents and students to lose confidence in educational fairness.

questions.q: Which body voided the initial NEET-UG 2026 results?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the National Testing Agency decided to void the initial results to maintain integrity and public trust.

questions.q: Which evidence was described as closely mirroring the actual NEET-UG 2026 test?
questions.explanation: Fraudulent 'guess papers' that closely mirrored the actual test were part of the evidence.

questions.q: What further application cost must candidates pay for the NEET-UG 2026 re-test?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the test will be administered again without candidates paying any further application costs.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The NEET-UG 2026 re-test will be held for all candidates.
Reason (R): The NEET-UG 2026 examination was officially cancelled.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.explanation: The booklet describes a planned re-sitting that follows the official cancellation, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Initial NEET-UG 2026 results   ->   A. Voided by the NTA
II. Re-test application cost   ->   B. No further payment required
III. Fraudulent 'guess papers'   ->   C. Closely mirrored the actual test
IV. Unauthorised exam material   ->   D. Circulated on digital platforms
questions.explanation: Each pair matches a fact the booklet states about the initial results, the re-test cost, the guess papers and the circulation of material.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The NEET-UG 2026 examination was officially cancelled.
II. The initial results were retained after the investigation.
III. Candidates must pay a fresh application fee for the re-test.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is supported, since the initial results were voided and no further application cost applies.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
The NTA voided the initial results.
The re-test is for all candidates.
A fee is payable for the re-test.
The fraudulent guess papers were part of the evidence.
questions.explanation: Three statements are correct, while the statement about a payable fee contradicts the booklet.

quizzes.title: NEET, NTA and the 2024 controversy: MCQ
quizzes.passage: NEET is the national entrance examination for admission into medical colleges across India, and it is conducted by the National Testing Agency. In 2024, an unusually high number of candidates achieved full marks, which drew attention to the examination. After the controversy that followed, the Ministry of Education formed a high-level committee to examine the matter. NEET 2026 was later declared compromised amid allegations of a paper leak, and the examination was officially cancelled. Authorities initiated an investigation after reports surfaced about illicit paper leaks and the circulation of unauthorised exam material. Evidence uncovered by law enforcement formed part of the investigation. The initial results were voided to maintain integrity and public trust, and candidates will take the test again without paying any further application costs. The decision reflects a commitment to fairness in high-stakes academic evaluations across the country. Exam cancellations delay admissions and disrupt the academic calendar for millions of students. Unfair practices cause significant stress, frustration and demotivation for ethical students. Large-scale cheating causes parents and students to lose confidence in educational fairness. Re-conducting compromised examinations imposes a heavy financial burden on government institutions. The Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act 2024 was introduced to curb paper leaks, organised cheating and manipulation in recruitment and entrance examinations.

questions.q: In which year was the National Testing Agency established?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the NTA was established in 2017.

questions.q: Who headed the high-level committee constituted after the NEET-UG 2024 controversy?
questions.explanation: The committee was headed by former ISRO Chairman Dr K Radhakrishnan.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the National Testing Agency located?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the NTA headquarters in New Delhi.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The NTA is an autonomous body under the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education.
Reason (R): The NTA conducts JEE Main and CUET.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.explanation: Both statements are true in the booklet, but conducting JEE Main and CUET does not explain the NTA's autonomous status.

questions.q:

III. Head of the NTA   ->   C. Pradeep Kumar Joshi
IV. Dr K Radhakrishnan   ->   D. Former ISRO Chairman
questions.explanation: Only two candidates scored full marks in 2023, no candidate did in 2022, Pradeep Kumar Joshi heads the NTA, and Dr K Radhakrishnan is a former ISRO Chairman.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The NTA was established in 2017.
II. The NTA headquarters is located in Mumbai.
III. The NTA conducts CUET.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I and statement III are correct, while the headquarters is in New Delhi, not Mumbai.

questions.q:

The NTA was established in 2014.
The NTA is an autonomous body under the Department of Higher Education.
The NTA conducts JEE Main.
Pradeep Kumar Joshi heads the NTA.
questions.explanation: The NTA was established in 2017, so only the other three statements are correct.
